title: Detect Squares
summary: Start with an empty point multiset.

contractDetails.constraints: 0–3000 operations. Coordinates are integers in [0,1000]. Duplicate additions are distinct choices. The query point does not need to be stored.

statement: Start with an empty point multiset. An operation [0,x,y] adds one copy of the point. An operation [1,x,y] asks how many ways three stored points and the query point form the four corners of an axis-aligned square with positive area. Return one answer per query, in order.

examples.explanation: The three stored corners complete the unit square.
A point alone cannot make a positive-area square.
Either stored copy of the horizontal partner can be used.

constraints: 0–3000 operations. Coordinates are integers in [0,1000]. Duplicate additions are distinct choices. The query point does not need to be stored.
hints: Conceptual: Choose a corner on the same row as the query to fix the side length.
Directional: For each horizontal partner, check the two possible vertical directions.
Implementation: Multiply the counts of the three required stored corners, then sum over eligible partners.
complexityAnalysis: O(1) per add and O(U) per count for a bounded coordinate row scan, with U=1001. A dense grid uses O(U²) space.
